seo.title: Case study: sneaker reseller stock in sync across StockX and Alias · Coelor
seo.description: How a Dutch sneaker reseller keeps StockX and Alias in sync with its warehouse: sold-out sizes switched off every 10 minutes, marketplace sales off the warehouse stock within minutes, 31,000+ sizes checked.

hero.headline: One stock count across StockX, Alias and the warehouse.
hero.sub: How a Dutch sneaker reseller stopped pausing sold-out sizes by hand and stopped typing marketplace sales into its warehouse system.

stats.label: until a sold-out size is off every marketplace

problem.headline: Every pair lives in several places at once.
problem.body: The same pair is listed size by size on StockX and Alias, in more than one region, while the real stock sits in the warehouse system. Every sale has to show up everywhere, fast.

items.title: Sold twice
items.body: A size sells on one marketplace and stays live on another. The second buyer gets a cancellation, and the marketplace counts it against you.

items.title: Sales typed over
items.body: Every marketplace sale is taken off the warehouse stock by hand before the count is right again.

items.title: Listings paused by hand
items.body: After each sale someone pauses the same size on the other accounts, one by one.

items.title: Sizes written ten ways
items.body: 9W, 9M, 38,5 and (GS): the same size is spelled differently in the warehouse and on each marketplace.

setup.headline: The warehouse is the single source of truth.
setup.body: Coelor sits between the marketplaces and the warehouse. It reads stock from the warehouse, switches off sold-out sizes on every marketplace account and brings every sale back.
before: Sold-out sizes paused by hand after each sale
Marketplace sales typed into the warehouse system
A size could sell twice before anyone noticed
after: EU and US sizes read from 31,000+ product names and linked
Sold-out sizes switched off on every account every 10 minutes
StockX and Alias sales off the warehouse stock within minutes
Every automatic delisting posted to the team chat

steps.title: Read and link every size
steps.body: EU and US sizes are read from each product name, more than 31,000 of them, and linked to the same size on StockX and Alias. Exceptions can be linked by hand.

steps.title: Switch off sold-out sizes
steps.body: Every 10 minutes the whole warehouse catalogue is checked, and any size with no free stock is switched off on every marketplace account.

steps.title: Bring every sale back
steps.body: StockX sales are picked up every 5 minutes and Alias sales every 7. Each one comes off the warehouse stock with its order number.

steps.title: Report and test every action
steps.body: Every automatic switch-off is posted to the team chat, and every change can run in test mode first.

fit.headline: Built for sneaker sellers who have outgrown manual work.
items: You sell on StockX, Alias or other marketplaces and on your own store
You keep stock per size in a warehouse or inventory system
You have hundreds or thousands of product and size combinations
Someone on your team pauses listings or types over sales every day

offer.title: How we start
items: A 30-minute call to map your channels and stock flow
A written scope and a fixed quote
Most builds run in 3 to 6 weeks, in test mode first

items.q: Do we have to change our webshop or warehouse system?
items.a: No. Coelor connects to the systems you already run through their APIs. If a system has no API, we work from its exports.
The build above connects StockX (EU and US) and Alias to Picqer and Google Sheets. We connect other marketplaces and shop systems through their APIs, or work from their exports.

items.q: What happens if a marketplace API goes down?
items.a: Runs back off and retry when a marketplace is slow or rate-limits. A sale is only marked as handled after it has come off the warehouse stock, so a failed run is picked up again on the next one.

items.q: Can we see what it will do before it changes anything?
items.a: Yes. Every change can run in test mode first, which logs what it would do without doing it.
Most builds take 3 to 6 weeks from the first call, including the dry-run period next to your team.
